title: Create an "AI Moderation" Explainer for Educators
description: Zedu’s philosophy is "AI should assist, not replace." Write a short, non-technical guide explaining how an educator can use Zedu's AI to summarize a week's worth of cohort discussions, saving them hours of reading.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: A plain-English guide to using Zedu AI summaries without giving up human judgement
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Write a short educator-facing explainer on using Zedu AI to summarise a week of cohort discussion. Cover what the summary is good for, what it can miss, how to check it against the thread, and when a human must step in. Use only AI capabilities that are visible on zedu.chat or in public help content; label anything unverified. Include a one-page checklist. One task: write the explainer and checklist.

tasks.title: Write the educator guide to Zedu AI summaries and the human-check checklist

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Show, don't tell: one synthetic week of cohort chat, its AI summary, and an annotated check
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Next to the plain-English guide, add a worked example educators can trust. Approach: in a test workspace, post a realistic synthetic week of cohort discussion (questions, a decision, an off-topic thread, one learner in difficulty), run Zedu's AI summary, and annotate the result: what it captured, what it missed or softened, and what the educator must still read themselves. Done: screenshots, the annotated summary, and three rules of thumb taken from what the test showed. No real learner data.
